description: The plot illustrates the similarity of HSAs in different languages across all layers within Qwen1.5-1.8B for four language pairs. The x-axis represents the layers, ranging from 0 to 23 with a linear scale and tick labels at intervals of 2, while the y-axis indicates similarity, ranging from 0.00 to 0.45 with a linear scale and tick labels at intervals of 0.05. The red line, representing 'en&en', starts at approximately 0.07 at layer 0, peaks at layer 6 with a value of 0.26, declines to 0.08 at layer 20, and then sharply increases to 0.43 at layer 23. The blue line, representing 'en&es', begins at 0.05 at layer 0, peaks at layer 6 with a value of 0.24, and then declines to 0.06 at layer 20 before increasing to 0.37 at layer 23. The green line, representing 'en&el', starts at 0.04 at layer 0, peaks at layer 6 with a value of 0.15, declines to 0.05 at layer 20, and then increases to 0.30 at layer 23. The pink line, representing 'en&bn', begins at 0.03 at layer 0, peaks at layer 6 with a value of 0.14, declines to 0.05 at layer 20, and then increases to 0.30 at layer 23. All lines exhibit a peak at layer 6, a decline thereafter, and a sharp increase at layer 23.
caption_used: The similarity of HSAs in different languages across all layers within Qwen1.5-1.8B is depicted. The line plot shows four language pairs: 'en&en' (red), 'en&es' (blue), 'en&el' (green), and 'en&bn' (pink). The horizontal axis represents the layers, ranging from 0 to 24, while the vertical axis indicates similarity, ranging from 0.00 to 0.45. The red line starts at approximately 0.07 at layer 0, peaks at layer 6 with a value of 0.26, and then declines steadily to 0.08 at layer 20 before sharply increasing to 0.43 at layer 23. The blue line begins at 0.06 at layer 0, peaks at layer 6 with a value of 0.24, and then stabilizes around 0.06 from layer 20 onward, showing no significant increase. The green and pink lines exhibit similar trends, starting at 0.04 and 0.03 respectively, peaking at layer 6 with values of 0.15 and 0.13, and then declining to 0.05 at layer 20 before increasing to 0.3 at layer 23. Notably, the similarity between 'en&es' consistently exceeds that of 'en&en' across layers 6 to 20, contrary to expectations.
